text:
A circular coil has moment of inertia $0.8 kg m^{2}$
 around any diameter and is carrying current to
produce a magnetic moment of $20 Am^{2}$
. The coil is kept initially in a vertical position and it can
rotate freely around a horizontal diameter. When a uniform magnetic field of 4 T is applied along the
vertical,it starts rotating around its horizontal diameter. The angular speed the coil acquires after
rotating by $60^{o}$ will be:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The magnetic moment $⃗{M}$ is normal to the plane of the coil. With the plane of the coil vertical, $⃗{M}$ is horizontal, at $90^{\circ }$ to the vertical field $⃗{B}$.

The torque turns $⃗{M}$ towards $⃗{B}$. After the coil rotates by $60^{\circ }$ about its horizontal diameter, the angle between $⃗{M}$ and $⃗{B}$ is $90^{\circ }-60^{\circ }=30^{\circ }$.

With $U=-MB\cos θ$ and the coil starting from rest, energy conservation gives

$\dfrac{1}{2}Iω^{2}=(-MB\cos 90^{\circ })-(-MB\cos 30^{\circ })=\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}MB$

$ω=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}MB}{I}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{\sqrt{3}\times 20\times 4}{0.8}}=\sqrt{100\sqrt{3}}=10(3)^{1/4}\text{rad s}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
A small ball of mass m is thrown upward with velocity u from the ground. The ball experiences a
resistive force mkv$^{2}$
 where v is its speed. The maximum height attained by the ball is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Taking upward as positive, both the weight $mg$ and the resistive force $mkv^{2}$ act downward while the ball rises.


[IMG]

$mv\dfrac{dv}{ds}=-mg-mkv^{2}\Rightarrow ds=-\dfrac{v~dv}{g+kv^{2}}$

At the maximum height $v=0$, so integrating from $v=u$ at $s=0$ to $v=0$ at $s=H$:

$H=\int\limits _{0}^{u}\dfrac{v~dv}{g+kv^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{2k}\left [\ln \left (g+kv^{2}\right )\right ]_{0}^{u}=\dfrac{1}{2k}\ln \left (\dfrac{g+ku^{2}}{g}\right )$

$H=\dfrac{1}{2k}\ln \left (1+\dfrac{ku^{2}}{g}\right )$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

Consider two uniform discs of the same thickness and different radii $R_{1}$
 = R and
 $R_{2}$
 = $α$R made of
the same material. If the ratio of their moments of inertia $I_{1}$

is $I_{1}$
 : $I_{2}$
 = 1 : 16 then the value of $α$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Moment of inertia of disc, $I=\frac{MR^{2}}{2}=\frac{\left [p\left (πR^{2}\right )t\right ]R^{2}}{2}$

$I=KR^{4}$

$\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=\left (\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}\right )^{4}$

$\frac{1}{16}=\left (\frac{R}{αR}\right )^{4}\Rightarrow α=(16)^{\frac{1}{4}}=2$

text:
A series L-R circuit is connected to a battery of emf V. If the circuit is switched on at t = 0, then
the time at which the energy stored in the inductor reaches $\left (\frac{1}{n}\right )$  times of its maximum value, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
P.E. in inductor, $U=\frac{1}{2}LI^{2}$

$U\propto I^{2}$

$\frac{U}{U_{0}}=\left (\frac{I}{I_{0}}\right )^{2}$

$\frac{1}{n}=\left (\frac{I}{I_{0}}\right )^{2}$

$I=\frac{I_{0}}{\sqrt{n}}$

We know, $I=I_{0}\left (1-e^{-\frac{R}{L}t}\right )$

$\frac{I_{0}}{\sqrt{n}}=I_{0}\left (1-e^{-\frac{R}{L}t}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $e^{-\frac{Rt}{L}}$ = 1 - $\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}$

taking ln & solving we get,

$t=\frac{L}{R}\ln \left (\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\sqrt{n}-1}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by

$\vec{E}=E_{0}\left (\widehat{x}+\hat{y}\right )\sin (kz-ωt)$

Its magnetic field will be given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\vec{E}=E_{0}\left (\widehat{x}+\hat{y}\right )\sin (kz-ωt)$

We know, direction of propagation, $\vec{C}=\vec{E}\times \vec{B}$

Here direction of propagation = $\widehat{k}$

$\therefore$ $\widehat{k}$ = $\vec{E}\times \vec{B}$

and $\widehat{E}=\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\widehat{k}=\left (\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}\right )\times \vec{B}$

 $\Rightarrow$ $\widehat{B}=\frac{-\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\widehat{B}$ = $\frac{E_{0}}{c}\left (-\widehat{x}+\hat{y}\right )\sin (kz-ωt)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
A cube of metal is subjected to a hydrostatic pressure of 4 GPa. The percentage change in the
length of the side of the cube is close to :

(Given bulk modulus of metal, B = 8 $\times$ $10^{10} Pa)$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Under a hydrostatic pressure $p$, the volume strain is $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=\dfrac{p}{B}$:

$\frac{\Delta V}{V}=\frac{4\times 10^{9}}{8\times 10^{10}}=0.05$

For a cube $V=L^{3}$, so $\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=3\dfrac{\Delta L}{L}$:

$\frac{\Delta L}{L}=\frac{0.05}{3}=\frac{1}{60}$

Percentage change in the side $=\dfrac{1}{60}\times 100\approx 1.67%$ (a decrease).

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

text:
A paramagnetic sample shows a net magnetisation of 6 A/m when it is placed in an external
magnetic field of 0.4 T at a temperature of 4 K. When the sample is placed in an external magnetic
field of 0.3 T at a temperature of 24 K, then the magnetisation will be:

$M=\frac{CB_{ext}}{T}$

$\Rightarrow C=60$

$\therefore$ Case - II : $M=\frac{60\times 0.3}{24}$ $=\frac{60\times 3}{240}=\frac{3}{4}=0.75A/m$

text:
A particle of charge q and mass m is subjected to an electric field
 $E = E_{0}$
 (1 – $ax^{2})$ in the x-direction,
where $a$ and $E_{0}$
 are constants. Initially the particle was at rest at x = 0. Other than the initial
position the kinetic energy of the particle becomes zero when the distance of the particle from the
origin is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$W=\Delta KE$

As inital and final kinetic energy both are zero so $\Delta KE$ = 0

$\therefore$ W = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\int\limits _{0}^{x}Fdx=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $q\int\limits _{0}^{x}E_{0}\left (1-ax^{2}\right )dx=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $qE_{0}\left [\int\limits _{0}^{x}dx-a\int\limits _{0}^{x}x^{2}dx\right ]=0$

$\RightarrowqE_{0}\left [x-\frac{ax^{3}}{3}\right ]=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x\left (1-\frac{ax^{2}}{3}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x=0,$ $1-\frac{ax^{2}}{3}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{ax^{2}}{3}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $x=\sqrt{\frac{3}{a}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

A capacitor C is fully charged with voltage $V_{0}$. After disconnecting the voltage source, it is connected

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

Heat loss = $\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{C_{1}C_{2}}{C_{1}+C_{2}}\right )V_{0}^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{C\times \frac{C}{2}}{C+\frac{C}{2}}\right )V_{0}^{2}$

= $\frac{1}{6}CV_{0}^{2}$

text:
Two identical cylindrical vessels are kept on the ground and each contain the same liquid of density
d. The area of the base of both vessels is S but the height of liquid in one vessel is $x_{1}$
 and in the
other, $x_{2}$
. When both cylinders are connected through a pipe of negligible volume very close to the
bottom, the liquid flows from one vessel to the other until it comes to equilibrium at a new height.
The change in energy of the system in the process is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$u_{i}=\left [dSx_{1}.\frac{x_{1}}{2}+dSx_{2}.\frac{x_{2}}{2}\right ]g\left \{dSx_{1}\to m,\frac{x_{1}}{2}\to h(C.O.M)\right \}$

Here total volume remains same.

$\therefore$ $V_{i} = V_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$ $S(x_{1} + x_{2}) = S(h + h)$

$\Rightarrow$ h = $\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}$

$u_{f} = ($dSh)g$\frac{h}{2}\times 2$

$\Rightarrow$ $u_{f}=\left [dS\left (\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}\right )\times \left (\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{4}\right )\times 2\right ]g$

$\therefore$ $u_{i}-u_{f}=dSg\left [\frac{x_{1}^{2}}{2}+\frac{x_{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(x_{1}+x_{2})^{2}}{4}\right ]$

$=dSg\frac{(x_{1}-x_{2})^{2}}{4}$

text:
The change in the magnitude of the volume of an ideal gas when a small additional pressure $\Delta$P is
applied at a constant temperature, is the same as the change when the temperature is reduced by
a small quantity $\Delta$T at constant pressure. The initial temperature and pressure of the gas were 300
K and 2 atm. respectively. 
If |$\Delta$T| = C|$\Delta$P| then value of C in (K/atm.) is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know, $PV=nRT$

$\therefore$ $P\Delta V+V\Delta P=0$ (for constant temp.)

and $P\Delta V$ = $nR\Delta T$ (for constant pressure)

$\Delta T=\frac{P\Delta V}{nR}$

$\Delta P=-\frac{P\Delta V}{V}$ ($\Delta V$ is same in both cases)

$\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta P}=\frac{P\Delta V}{nR}\frac{V}{-P\Delta V}=\frac{-V}{nR}=-\frac{T}{P}$

[As PV = nRT

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{V}{nR}=\frac{T}{P}$]

$\therefore$ $\left |\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta P}\right |=\left |\frac{-300}{2}\right |=150$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot

solution.body:

or $\sin θ=\frac{nλ}{d}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{nλ}{d}\leq 1$

$n\leq 100$

For both sides 100 + 100 = 200

text:
The distance between an object and a screen is 100 cm. A lens can produce real image of the
object on the screen for two different positions between the screen and the object. The distance
between these two positions is 40 cm. If the power of the lens is close to $\left (\frac{N}{100}\right )D$ where N is an
integer, the value of N is $_________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using displacement method

$f=\frac{D^{2}-d^{2}}{4D}$

Here, D = 100 cm

and d = 40 cm

$f=\frac{100^{2}-40^{2}}{4(100)}=21cm$

$P=\frac{1}{f}=\frac{100}{21}D$

$\frac{N}{100}=\frac{100}{21}$

$N=476$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 4th September Evening Slot
